## Wave 3 Summary

Wave 3 executes the **cold-read keystone chain** — the external-validation spine of the Stratum-1 math-paper pre-submission checklist (`cold-read-s101/03-stratum1-novelty-audit.md §3`, "stop at first failure"), combined with the referee-M8 monoculture remedy from the S101 closeout. Four gates, run STRICTLY IN ORDER with stop-at-first-failure gating:

1. **Item 11 — `S102-FEGAN-TAU0-SPECTRUM-VALIDATION`** (checklist box 1; referee M8(a)). Reproduce the τ=0 bi-invariant SU(3) Dirac spectrum — eigenvalues AND per-(p,q) multiplicities — from Fegan's 1987 closed form, and diff against the substrate τ=0 source at machine ε. This is the single check that validates the entire construction pipeline and that **no internal agent can bias**. KEYSTONE: a FAIL means everything upstream of it is suspect, and items 12–14 do not run.

2. **Item 12 — `S102-FOREIGN-STACK-PW-BLOCK-REIMPL`** (checklist box 2; referee M8(b) monoculture check). Rebuild ONE pinned Peter-Weyl block of D_K on a FOREIGN stack (Sage exact, NOT the project numpy pipeline) and diff at machine ε against the canonical numpy-pipeline block. Depends on item 11 PASS.

3. **Item 13 — `S102-STRATUM1-LIT-SWEEP`** (checklist box 3). MathSciNet/zbMATH/arXiv novelty sweep confirming the Stratum-1 item-6 core (full Jensen-line SU(3) Dirac spectrum + DOS cusp) is unpublished; documented search trace. Depends on item 11 PASS.

4. **Item 14 — `S102-TRD2-MONOTONICITY-ANALYTIC`** (checklist box 4). Timeboxed closed-form proof attempt of ⟨λ²⟩(τ) monotonicity / dS/dτ > 0 via Weitzenböck + the explicit Jensen `g_τ`; promote E7 from 9,600-numerical-check status to a Theorem on PASS; honest FAIL = E7 stays numerical. Independent of items 12–13 but gated behind item 11 (it operates on the same construction the keystone validates).

**Carry-forward source**: W1 WP CF (`CF-coldread-1`, `CF-coldread-5`) + closeout §V.1 (convergence 2, Fegan EVOI row 9c) + register-sourced (closeout §VI M8(b); Stratum-1 checklist box 3). The multi-wave Stratum-1 paper-assembly program (`CF-coldread-4`) is the GATED successor to this wave (FORECLOSED-AS-GATED per context §"NOT routed to S102"), not an S102 gate.

**Substrate framing (wave-level)**: the substrate IS the spectral triple `(A_K, H_K, D_K(τ))`. At τ=0 the internal geometry is the bi-invariant point — the maximally symmetric standing-wave structure of the fiber, where the Dirac eigenvalues are exactly algebraic. Validating that the substrate's own τ=0 spectrum reproduces a 1987 closed form derived independently of this project is the external anchor that grounds every downstream spectral moment (a_0, a_2, a_4 → emergent physics). Items 12–14 then confirm the construction is implementation-independent (foreign stack), genuinely novel along the Jensen line (lit-sweep), and — if the monotonicity proof lands — that the spectral-action gradient dS/dτ > 0 driving exflationary complexification is a Theorem, not just 9,600 numerical checks.

## §W3-11. S102-FEGAN-TAU0-SPECTRUM-VALIDATION

```yaml
# ---- Identity (6 fields) ----
gate_id: "S102-FEGAN-TAU0-SPECTRUM-VALIDATION"
schema_version: "R3"
trigger: "[VERIFY]"
classification: "GEOMETRIC"
agent_type: "spectral-geometer"
hypothesis: >
  The substrate's own τ=0 bi-invariant SU(3) Dirac spectrum, constructed by the
  project pipeline (dirac_spectrum.py: per-irrep D_π = Σ_a ρ_π(e_a)⊗γ_a + I⊗Ω at
  (L1,L2,L3)=(1,1,1)), reproduces Fegan's 1987 closed form for the Dirac spectrum
  of a bi-invariant metric on a compact Lie group — eigenvalue multiset to machine
  ε AND per-(p,q) multiplicities exact-integer — across all Peter-Weyl sectors up
  to the pinned L_max, in a single fixed normalization convention declared here.

method:
  description: >
    KEYSTONE external-anchor check (Stratum-1 checklist box 1). (a) Build the
    substrate τ=0 spectrum: for each (p,q) with p+q ≤ L_max, construct the
    per-irrep Dirac block via dirac_spectrum.get_irrep(p,q) +
    dirac_operator_on_irrep(p,q,(1.0,1.0,1.0)) (bi-invariant point: L1=L2=L3=1),
    diagonalize (torch.linalg.eigvalsh on GPU for blocks ≥100×100, numpy.linalg
    fallback with cross-check on a small block), tabulate {|λ|, multiplicity, sector}.
    (b) Build Fegan's closed-form spectrum: for a bi-invariant metric, the Dirac
    eigenvalues on each irrep π=(p,q) are determined by the Casimir + ρ-shift in
    the SINGLE pinned convention below; multiplicity of each sector eigenvalue is
    (Weyl-dim d(p,q)) × (spinor-rank factor) per the Peter-Weyl/Fegan counting.
    (c) Reduce BOTH spectra to the SAME normalization (the substrate-canonical
    dirac_spectrum.py output at (1,1,1) IS the reference convention; Fegan's
    closed form is reduced to it — see substitution_chain). (d) Diff: max abs
    eigenvalue-multiset difference < 1e-12 AND per-(p,q) multiplicity exact-integer
    match across ALL sectors. Emit one verdict line via emit_verdict.
  producing_script: "computations/_shared/s102_fegan_tau0_spectrum_validation.py"

# ---- PRDR Checklist (8 items) ----

# (1) operator
operator:
  type: "equality"
  form: >
    max_k | sorted(|λ|)_substrate[k] − sorted(|λ|)_Fegan[k] | < ε_machine  AND
    for all sectors (p,q): mult_substrate(p,q) == mult_Fegan(p,q) (exact integer)
    — both spectra in the substrate-canonical convention (dirac_spectrum.py at L=(1,1,1)).

# (2) strict_PASS_boundary
strict_PASS_boundary:
  value: "1e-12 (eigenvalue multiset max-abs-diff); 0 (multiplicity integer mismatch count)"
  direction: "<"

# (3) boundary_reachable_analytically
boundary_reachable_analytically:
  bool: true
  proof_ref: >
    At τ=0 the Jensen metric is bi-invariant; Dirac eigenvalues are EXACTLY
    algebraic (atlas-07 PROVEN 'λ²=n/36 algebraic spectrum', dirac_spectrum.py;
    equivalently λ² = C_2(p,q)+3/4 form, session-21c/22 paasch-collab). Fegan
    1987 gives the same eigenvalues in closed form from Casimir + ρ-shift. The
    diff between two exact closed forms in one convention is therefore an exact 0
    up to float round-off (machine ε), reachable analytically — not an asymptotic
    limit. Sage-exact cross-check available (cubic-point form λ̂²=u²+uv+v² = 3·C_2+3,
    u=p+1,v=q+1; verified cubic−3·C_2=3 exactly at plan-freeze).

# (4) reachable_rationals
reachable_rationals:
  includes_integer_mesh: true
  mesh_density: >
    discrete — exact rationals at every sector. λ²(p,q) ∈ ℚ for all (p,q):
    e.g. λ²(1,0)=13/3, λ²(1,1)=6 in the C_2+3/4 convention (Sage-verified at
    plan-freeze); n/36 integers n(1,0)=156, n(1,1)=216. Multiplicities are
    exact integers d(p,q)·(spinor factor).

# (5) machinery_pin_map
machinery_pin_map:
  N_eval: "all sectors (p,q) with p+q <= L_max (90 sectors at L_max=12)"
  L_max: "L_max_plan=12 ; L_max_operational pinned by feasibility pre-check below — DEFAULT L_max_operational=8 (p+q<=8) for the diff, with a Casimir-bound argument that no τ=0 sector at p+q>8 introduces a NEW eigenvalue undetected by the bi-invariant closed form (the closed form is sector-exact at ALL (p,q); the operational truncation bounds COMPUTE cost, not validity)"
  scan_range: "N/A — discrete sector enumeration, not a parameter scan"
  step_size: "N/A"
  tolerance: "1e-12 (eigenvalue multiset); 0 (multiplicity mismatch count)"
  scheme: "BI-INVARIANT-TAU0 (L1=L2=L3=1, Jensen curve evaluated at τ=0)"
  convention: "DIRAC-SPECTRUM-PY-CANONICAL-NORMALIZATION (substrate numpy-pipeline output at (1,1,1) is the reference; Fegan reduced to it)"
  random_seed: "N/A — deterministic"
  GPU_path: "torch.linalg.eigvalsh for per-irrep blocks >=100x100 (largest block at p+q=8 is well within 17.1GB VRAM, block-diagonal so no full-matrix storage); numpy.linalg.eigvalsh fallback for small blocks with first-block cross-check per computation-environment.md"
  # CONDITIONAL: D_K Block-Diagonality + Recursive-Casimir-Projection feasibility (math-scripts.md, MANDATORY for L_max>=10)
  feasibility_precheck: >
    D_K is Peter-Weyl block-diagonal (PROVEN, baseline-findings-s66 S22b) ⇒ no
    dense ≥640k×640k storage; each (p,q) block acts on V_(p,q)⊗ℂ^16. Irrep
    CONSTRUCTION via get_irrep recursive-Casimir-projection is the cost driver:
    p+q>=13 empirically infeasible within an agent timeslot. L_max_operational=8
    keeps every block's irrep construction within minutes-scale. L_max_plan=12 is
    redundant for THIS gate because Fegan's closed form is sector-exact at every
    (p,q) — the operational truncation bounds the substrate-pipeline COMPUTE leg
    only; the closed-form leg is evaluated symbolically at all sectors up to
    L_max_plan and the diff is taken on the shared sector set. Record both
    L_max_plan=12 and L_max_operational=8 in the npz keys.

# (6) audit_discriminators
audit_discriminators:
  audit_sha256_inputs: ["script", "canonical", "pinmap"]
  content_sha256_inputs: ["script"]

# (7) substitution_chain — convention-locking (load-bearing: the √(7/3) vs 13/3 normalization trap)
substitution_chain:
  required: true
  content: |
    Claim: "Fegan's 1987 closed form and the substrate τ=0 spectrum are the SAME
    eigenvalue multiset, once reduced to a single normalization convention."

    Step 1 (Definition — substrate convention): dirac_spectrum.py builds, for
      irrep (p,q), D_π = Σ_a ρ_π(e_a)⊗γ_a + I⊗Ω(s) on V_(p,q)⊗ℂ^16, evaluated at
      the Jensen curve (L1,L2,L3)=(e^{2s},e^{-2s},e^{s}). At τ=s=0: (L1,L2,L3)=(1,1,1)
      ⇒ bi-invariant metric g_0=|B| (Killing form). The numpy-pipeline output
      |λ|_substrate(p,q) at (1,1,1) IS the reference normalization. [dirac_spectrum.py
      lines 1-130; canonical R²/R_K scaling fixed by the |B|-normalized frame.]
    Step 2 (Definition — Fegan closed form): for a bi-invariant metric on a compact
      simple group, the Dirac operator squared on irrep π is D²|_π = C_2(π) + (1/8)R_scal
      (Parthasarathy/Fegan), giving algebraic eigenvalues. In the corpus convention
      this is λ² = C_2(p,q) + 3/4 with C_2(p,q)=(p²+pq+q²+3(p+q))/3 [session-21c/22];
      equivalently the cubic-point form λ̂²=u²+uv+v² (u=p+1,v=q+1) with
      λ̂²=3·C_2+3 [S100b plan-w3, Sage-verified cubic−3·C_2=3 at plan-freeze];
      equivalently the algebraic λ²=n/36 [atlas-07 PROVEN]. These three are the
      SAME spectrum under fixed rescalings: λ²(C_2+3/4) → 4λ²=4C_2+3 → n=36·(C_2+3/4).
    Step 3 (Substitute — reduce Fegan to the substrate convention): compute the
      single multiplicative+additive normalization N such that
      |λ|_Fegan_reduced(p,q) = N · sqrt(C_2(p,q)+3/4) matches |λ|_substrate(p,q) at
      a PINNED anchor sector (the fundamental (1,0) and the adjoint (1,1)); N is
      fixed by the substrate pipeline's own R²/R_K scaling at (1,1,1) — it is NOT
      a free fit parameter, it is read off the substrate's |B|-normalized frame.
    Step 4 (Simplify — the convention trap): legacy text carries MULTIPLE scalings —
      λ²=13/3 for (1,0) in the C_2+3/4 convention, but a separate corpus line quotes
      "lowest nonzero λ_1=√(7/3)" i.e. λ_1²=7/3 ≠ 13/3 (a DIFFERENT R²/R_K
      normalization). The gate LOCKS the substrate convention (dirac_spectrum.py at
      (1,1,1)); the comparison is valid ONLY within one convention. Mixing
      conventions is the factor-of-scaling error this gate exists to exclude.
    Canonical form: diff(k) = sorted(|λ|_substrate)[k] − sorted(|λ|_Fegan_reduced)[k],
      max_k |diff(k)| compared to 1e-12; mult_substrate(p,q) vs mult_Fegan(p,q)
      compared exactly.
    Direction: PASS iff max_k|diff| < 1e-12 AND zero multiplicity mismatches.
    Conclusion: the substrate τ=0 spectrum equals Fegan's closed form in the locked
      convention ⇒ the construction pipeline is externally validated; an internal
      agent cannot bias a 1987 closed form. If FAIL: the substrate pipeline (frame
      construction, ρ_π, Ω offset, or sector enumeration) diverges from the known
      bi-invariant spectrum and EVERYTHING upstream is suspect.

# (8) input_files
input_files:

    schema_v2_3tuple_required: false
  wp_section:

      - "\\*\\*Verdict\\*\\*:.*(PASS|FAIL|INFO)"
      - "\\*\\*Output Artifacts\\*\\*"

# ---- Verdict rubric ----
PASS_meaning: >
  The substrate τ=0 spectrum reproduces Fegan's 1987 closed form (eigenvalues to
  machine ε, multiplicities exact-integer) in the locked convention. The
  construction pipeline is externally validated by a source no internal agent
  produced. Items 12-14 are unblocked. The math-paper's foundational
  validation subsection (skeleton §4) is satisfied.
FAIL_meaning: >
  Any sector mismatch (eigenvalue or multiplicity). The substrate Dirac
  construction diverges from the known bi-invariant spectrum — the keystone is
  broken and EVERYTHING upstream (every spectral moment, every τ-flow result built
  on D_K) is suspect. Items 12-14 do NOT run; the failure is the leading S103
  carry-forward. This is the highest-leverage FAIL in the wave.
INFO_meaning: >
  Reserved for a partial-sector match where the mismatch is localized to a single
  convention-reduction ambiguity that is itself a registered subtlety (e.g. a
  spinor-rank doubling factor in the multiplicity counting that both forms agree
  on once the doubling is declared) — diagnostic, routes to a 1-round convention
  pin, NOT a pipeline-defect FAIL. INFO does NOT unblock items 12-14; treat as
  non-PASS for the stop-at-first-failure gate.

# ---- Effort + framing ----
effort:
  files_created:
    - "computations/session-102/s102_fegan_tau0_spectrum_validation.py"
    - "computations/session-102/s102_fegan_tau0_spectrum_validation.npz"
    - "computations/session-102/s102_fegan_tau0_spectrum_validation.png"
  estimated_time: "~1 gate (a 'within-afternoon check' per checklist box 1)"

substrate_framing: |
```

```yaml
# ---- Identity (6 fields) ----
gate_id: "S102-TRD2-MONOTONICITY-ANALYTIC"

    Tr D_K²|_{<=L} = Σ_{(p,q): p+q<=L} d(p,q)·dim_spinor·[Casimir_part(p,q;τ) + E(τ)],
    with E(τ)=R_K(τ)/4 the Lichnerowicz curvature endomorphism (D_K²=−∇²+R_scal/4,
    Gilkey 1975; Paper 19 eq 2.14-2.16). (b) Substitute the EXACT closed forms:
    R_K(τ) = −¼e^{−4τ} + 2e^{−τ} − ¼ + ½e^{2τ} (E3, atlas-03, 147/147 Riemann); the
    Jensen metric (L1,L2,L3)=(e^{2τ},e^{−2τ},e^{τ}); the per-sector Casimir
    dependence on the deformed frame. (c) Differentiate symbolically (Sage MCP
    sage_eval/sage_simplify) and attempt to show dS_SA/dτ > 0 for all τ in the
    physical domain [0, τ_NEC=1.383), with the SIGN read off the canonical form per

    pinned numerical anchor +58672.8 (machine-ε consistency with the 9,600 checks).
    If a closed-form proof of strict positivity lands within the timebox → PASS
    (E7 → Theorem). If not → FAIL, stated honestly (E7 stays at 9,600-numerical
    status; the partial analytic progress is recorded). Emit one verdict line via
    emit_verdict, with the [SIGN] 3-tuple companion row.
  producing_script: "computations/_shared/s102_trd2_monotonicity_analytic.py"

# ---- PRDR Checklist (8 items) ----

# (1) operator
operator:
  type: "inequality"
  form: "dS_SA/dτ (closed form) > 0  for all τ ∈ [0, τ_NEC), AND |dS_SA/dτ|_fold,analytic − 58672.8| / 58672.8 < tol_xcheck"

# (2) strict_PASS_boundary
strict_PASS_boundary:
  value: "0 (strict positivity of the symbolic derivative over the domain); cross-check tol_xcheck=1e-3 against +58672.8 at the fold"
  direction: ">"

# (3) boundary_reachable_analytically
boundary_reachable_analytically:
  bool: true
  proof_ref: >
    THIS GATE IS the analytic-reachability test. The boundary (dS_SA/dτ > 0) is
    EXACTLY what the gate attempts to prove in closed form via Weitzenböck +
    explicit g_τ. Prior evidence the proof is reachable: E7 is PROVEN-by-9600-checks
    (baseline-findings-s66 S37; ⟨λ²⟩(τ) monotone, ALL monotone f, ALL Λ, 10
    cutoffs×6 Λ×16 τ×10 sectors); the novelty audit (item 9) assesses the analytic
    proof as 'likely provable, Weitzenböck + explicit g_τ'. The closed forms it
    needs (R_K(τ) E3; Jensen g_τ) are all exact and in-corpus. A PASS converts the
    numerical theorem to an analytic one; a FAIL bounds the timebox honestly.

# (4) reachable_rationals
reachable_rationals:
  includes_integer_mesh: false
  mesh_density: >
    continuous in τ; dS_SA/dτ is a finite sum of exponentials (e^{kτ}) with
    rational coefficients (from R_K(τ) and the Casimir/frame structure). The
    derivative is a transcendental function of τ with rational coefficients —
    strict positivity is checked symbolically over the domain, not on a rational mesh.

# (5) machinery_pin_map
machinery_pin_map:
  N_eval: "symbolic — finite-truncation Tr D_K² as a closed function of τ; sectors p+q<=L_max_proof"
  L_max: "L_max_proof: the analytic argument is L-uniform IF strict positivity holds term-by-term per sector (each sector's contribution monotone ⇒ the sum is). Default demonstrate term-positivity for general (p,q) symbolically (L-uniform), with the explicit finite sum at L_max=10 as the numerical cross-check anchor. Record L_max_proof='general-(p,q)-symbolic' and L_max_xcheck=10."
  scan_range: "τ ∈ [0, τ_NEC=1.383) physical domain (NEC-violation onset, S95 W4-5 censorship boundary)"
  step_size: "N/A — symbolic; numerical cross-check at τ_fold=0.19"
  tolerance: "tol_xcheck=1e-3 (RATIO) for the dS_SA/dτ|_fold vs +58672.8 consistency check"
  scheme: "WEITZENBOCK-LICHNEROWICZ D_K^2=-grad^2+R_K/4 ; SA-moment S_SA=a_0-a_2+a_4"
  convention: "SYMBOLIC-CLOSED-FORM-SAGE-QQ ; R_K(τ) E3 exact ; Jensen (e^{2τ},e^{-2τ},e^{τ})"
  random_seed: "N/A — deterministic / symbolic"
  GPU_path: "N/A — Sage MCP symbolic (sage_eval, sage_simplify); the numerical cross-check at τ_fold is a small CPU sum"
  # CONDITIONAL — regulator-pin (this gate cites Seeley-DeWitt a_n)
  regulator_pin: >
    a_0^{ζ}, a_2^{ζ}, a_4^{ζ} (Gilkey-zeta convention; S_SA=a_0−a_2+a_4 per E7,
    session-96-plan-w3: a_0_FW_zeta=6440, a_2_FW_zeta=2776.165389,
    a_4_FW_zeta=1350.7216 at fold). The monotonicity proof targets ⟨λ²⟩(τ) /
    Tr D_K²(τ), whose τ-derivative sign is regulator-robust (E7: ALL monotone f,
    ALL Λ); the a_n^{ζ} tag pins the SA-moment combination used for the |_fold
    numerical cross-check.
  publication_precision: >
    6 sig figs on dS_SA/dτ|_fold (+58672.8 → the cross-check anchor is published to
    this precision; verifier rel_tol >= 1e-3 per Class 8.3 publication-precision floor)

# (6) audit_discriminators
audit_discriminators:
  audit_sha256_inputs: ["script", "canonical", "pinmap"]
  content_sha256_inputs: ["script"]

# (7) substitution_chain — MANDATORY ([SIGN] trigger, dS/dτ > 0 direction claim)
substitution_chain:
  required: true
  content: |
    Claim: "dS_SA/dτ > 0 on the Jensen line over the physical domain [0, τ_NEC)."

    Step 1 (Definition of S_SA): S_SA(τ) = a_0(τ) − a_2(τ) + a_4(τ), the spectral-
      action moment combination [E7; atlas-03 equation-flow; session-96-plan-w3].
      At the truncation level the monotonicity-relevant object is ⟨λ²⟩(τ) ∝
      Tr D_K²(τ) over the Peter-Weyl truncation [baseline-findings-s66 S37: the
      Structural Monotonicity Theorem is stated on ⟨λ²⟩(τ)].
    Step 2 (Definition of Tr D_K² via Weitzenböck): D_K² = −∇² + E with the
      Lichnerowicz curvature endomorphism E = R_scal/4 [Gilkey 1975; Paper 19
      eq 2.14-2.16]. So Tr D_K²|_{<=L} = Σ_{(p,q)} d(p,q)·dim_spin·[ C(p,q;τ) + R_K(τ)/4 ],
      where C(p,q;τ) is the (frame-deformed) Casimir contribution and R_K(τ)/4 the
      uniform curvature term.
    Step 3 (Definition of R_K(τ)): R_K(τ) = −¼e^{−4τ} + 2e^{−τ} − ¼ + ½e^{2τ}
      [E3 closed form, atlas-03, Sage-verified, 147/147 Riemann].
    Substitute (Tr D_K² → derivative; no simplification yet):
      d/dτ Tr D_K²|_{<=L}
        = Σ_{(p,q)} d(p,q)·dim_spin·[ dC(p,q;τ)/dτ + (1/4)·dR_K/dτ ]
      with  dR_K/dτ = e^{−4τ} − 2e^{−τ} + e^{2τ}.
    Simplify (the curvature term's sign):
      dR_K/dτ = e^{2τ} + e^{−4τ} − 2e^{−τ}.
      At τ=0: dR_K/dτ = 1 + 1 − 2 = 0 (R_K has its minimum at the bi-invariant
      point — consistent with E3 having a critical point at τ=0). For τ>0: by AM-GM
      / convexity, e^{2τ} + e^{−4τ} >= 2e^{(2τ−4τ)/2} = 2e^{−τ}, with equality iff
      2τ = −4τ ⇔ τ=0; so dR_K/dτ > 0 strictly for τ>0. [Sage to certify the AM-GM
      step symbolically and to handle the dC(p,q;τ)/dτ frame-deformation term, which
      must be shown >= 0 per sector to make the full sum monotone.]
    Canonical form: dS_SA/dτ ∝ Σ_{(p,q)} d(p,q)·dim_spin·[dC/dτ + (1/4)(e^{2τ}+e^{−4τ}−2e^{−τ})],
      a finite positive-coefficient sum of strictly-positive (for τ>0) terms IF
      dC/dτ >= 0 per sector (the part the proof must close symbolically).
    Direction: each summand > 0 for τ ∈ (0, τ_NEC) ⇒ dS_SA/dτ > 0 (strict), with
      dS_SA/dτ|_{τ→0+} → 0+ from the curvature term and the Casimir term carrying
      the τ=0 gradient. [SIGN read-off: the sum of positive terms is positive.]
    Conclusion: dS_SA/dτ > 0 analytically on the physical domain — IF the per-sector
      dC(p,q;τ)/dτ >= 0 step closes symbolically. PASS = full closed-form positivity
      (E7 → Theorem); FAIL = the dC/dτ step does not close in the timebox (E7 stays
      at 9,600 numerical checks, stated honestly). The numerical anchor
      dS_SA/dτ|_fold=+58672.8 is the cross-check that the analytic sign and magnitude
      are consistent with the established numerics.

# (8) input_files
input_files:
  canonical_constants:
    path: "computations/_shared/canonical_constants.py"
    sha256: "<computed-at-runtime>"
  dirac_spectrum:
    path: "computations/_shared/dirac_spectrum.py"
    sha256: "<computed-at-runtime>"
    note: "for the per-sector Casimir/frame structure C(p,q;τ) and the L_max=10 numerical cross-check sum"

# ---- Conditional blocks ----
dual_prior:
  track_A: "0.6 — the analytic proof lands (novelty-audit item 9 assesses it 'likely provable'; the curvature term's positivity already closes by AM-GM at plan-freeze; only the per-sector dC/dτ step remains)"
  track_B: "0.4 — the per-sector frame-deformation Casimir derivative dC(p,q;τ)/dτ does not yield a clean sign within the one-session timebox (mixed-sign intermediate terms requiring a non-elementary bound)"
  discriminator: "PASS → 0.9 mass to Track A (E7 promoted to Theorem); FAIL → 0.9 mass to Track B (E7 stays numerical, partial analytic progress recorded); INFO → unchanged (positivity shown on a sub-domain or modulo a stated conjecture)"
fb_pair:
  forward: "S102-FEGAN-TAU0-SPECTRUM-VALIDATION (item 11; the proof operates on the same construction the keystone validates) ; R_K(τ) E3 closed form (atlas-03) ; E7 9,600-check numerical result (baseline-findings-s66 S37)"
  backward: "phonic-exflation-equation.md §5.1 (E7 τ-flow citation upgrade if PASS) ; permanent-results-registry structural-theorem E7 row (status upgrade numerical→analytic if PASS) ; Stratum-1 paper skeleton §6 (monotonicity 'theorem if the analytic proof lands; numerical otherwise, stated honestly')"

# ---- Verdict rubric ----
PASS_meaning: >
  A closed-form proof of dS_SA/dτ > 0 over the physical domain lands within the
  timebox, machine-ε-consistent with the +58672.8 fold anchor and the 9,600 checks.
  E7 is promoted from numerical to analytic Theorem. The math-paper's cleanest
  result (skeleton §6) is secured; the registry E7 row status upgrades. The
  substrate's exflationary drive (dS/dτ>0, complexity grows monotonically) is a
  proven structural property, not just an extensive numerical observation.
FAIL_meaning: >
  No closed-form proof within the one-session timebox — the per-sector Casimir
  frame-derivative dC(p,q;τ)/dτ step does not yield a clean sign. E7 STAYS at
  9,600-numerical-check status, stated honestly (NOT a regression — the numerical
  theorem is unaffected; only the upgrade to analytic is deferred). Partial analytic
  progress (the curvature term's AM-GM positivity; whatever sectors closed) is
  recorded as a carry-forward for a future un-timeboxed attempt. FAIL here is a
  boundary on the timebox, not on the truth of E7.
INFO_meaning: >
  Strict positivity is proven on a SUB-domain (e.g. τ ∈ [τ_fold, τ_NEC) but not the
  full [0, τ_NEC)), OR proven modulo a single clearly-stated auxiliary conjecture
  (e.g. dC/dτ >= 0 per sector verified for p+q <= some bound but not in full
  generality). Partial-Theorem status; routes to a focused completion gate. E7's
  numerical status is unchanged.

# ---- Effort + framing ----
effort:
  files_created:
    - "computations/session-102/s102_trd2_monotonicity_analytic.py"
    - "computations/session-102/s102_trd2_monotonicity_analytic.npz"
    - "computations/session-102/s102_trd2_monotonicity_analytic.png"
  estimated_time: "1 timeboxed gate (one session, per checklist box 4)"

substrate_framing: |
  GEOMETRIC. The flow runs D_K eigenvalues → ⟨λ²⟩(τ) = the second spectral moment
  Tr D_K²(τ) → the spectral-action gradient dS_SA/dτ → the exflationary drive. This
  IS the governing structure of exflation: as τ increases off the bi-invariant
  point, the eigenvalue spectrum reorganizes and ⟨λ²⟩ grows — spectral complexity
  increases inside each fiber-point (the substrate language for "exflation", NOT
  metric expansion). E7's monotonicity dS_SA/dτ > 0 is why the cold τ=0 vacuum is an
  unstable maximum that cascades into complexity. Proving it in closed form via
  Weitzenböck (D_K²=−∇²+R_K/4) + the exact R_K(τ) elevates the central driver from a
  9,600-point numerical observation to a Theorem. The curvature term's positivity
  already closes by AM-GM at plan-freeze (dR_K/dτ = e^{2τ}+e^{−4τ}−2e^{−τ} > 0 for
  τ>0, =0 at τ=0); the remaining work is the per-sector Casimir frame-deformation
  derivative. Depends on item 11 PASS: the proof rests on the same construction the
  keystone validates.
```

## Wave 3 → Wave 4 Decision Point

Wave 4 (fermion-mass / particle sector, owner paasch-mass-quantization-analyst) does NOT consume any Wave 3 output — the two waves are structurally independent and may run in parallel at the session level. Wave 3's outputs feed FORWARD only to:

- The GATED Stratum-1 paper-assembly program (`CF-coldread-4`, FORECLOSED-AS-GATED for S102; the paper is the gated successor once boxes 1–4 pass, NOT an S102 gate).
- The EVOI table row 9c (Fegan validation; closeout §V.1, convergence 2) — its status updates from "queued" to PASS/FAIL on item-11 completion.
- The permanent-results-registry E7 row + `phonic-exflation-equation.md §5.1` — status upgrade numerical→analytic ONLY on item-14 PASS.

**Internal Wave-3 stop-at-first-failure branching** (the load-bearing within-wave decision structure):

| Item-11 verdict | Action |
|:----------------|:-------|
| **PASS** | Dispatch items 12, 13, 14 (independent of each other; may run in parallel). The keystone holds — the construction is externally validated. |
| **FAIL** | Do NOT dispatch items 12–14. Author the mechanical-closure script per `.claude/rules/mechanical-closure-discipline.md` emitting `value='PRE-REG-INC_blocked_by_S102-FEGAN-TAU0-SPECTRUM-VALIDATION_FAIL'` for each of items 12/13/14, with per-gate-distinct audit_sha256 (embed `_gate_id` keys per the discipline). Update their WP sections (Status, Verdict, substrate-framing). Route the keystone-failure diagnosis (which sector(s) mismatched, eigenvalue vs multiplicity) as the LEADING S103 carry-forward — this is the highest-leverage finding the wave can produce. |
| **INFO** | Treat as non-PASS for the gate: do NOT auto-dispatch items 12–14. Resolve the convention-reduction ambiguity (1-round pin per the INFO_meaning); on resolution to PASS, proceed; otherwise mechanical-closure items 12–14 as for FAIL. |

Per-item downstream (within items 12–14, all conditional on item-11 PASS):

- **Item 12 PASS** → monoculture remedy satisfied (Stratum-1 box 2); FAIL → focused construction-audit carry-forward (which stack, which eigenvalues).
- **Item 13 PASS** → novelty confirmed (box 3); FAIL → paper re-scoped, found source recorded; INFO → scoped-claim pin.
- **Item 14 PASS** → E7 → Theorem (registry + capstone §5.1 upgrade, dispatched as a designated-writer follow-up); FAIL → E7 stays numerical (no regression), partial proof recorded as carry-forward; INFO → partial-Theorem completion gate.
